# Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna (Tha-Ap 20)

**ID:** Tha-Ap 20

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 20) is a verse narrative within the Therāpadāna of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya, recording the past karmic deeds and biographical legend of the elder Raṭṭhapāla [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].

A full parallel to the poem is preserved later in the same collection as Tha-Ap 563 (*Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna*) [SuttaCentral]. The traditions regarding Raṭṭhapāla (Sanskrit: Rāṣṭrapāla) are widely represented across early Buddhist literature: the narrative figure corresponds to the protagonist of the *Raṭṭhapāla Sutta* (MN 82), with parallel traditions preserved in the Chinese Madhyama Āgama (MĀ 132), separate Chinese translations (T 68, T 69), the Sanskrit *Avadānaśataka* (Avs 90), fragments from the Turfan collection (SHT Sutta 18), and the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D 1) [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus document 159 matching passages across 24 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus and SuttaCentral agree on the near-verbatim duplicate in the Therāpadāna: segments §0.3–14.4 match Tha-Ap 563 almost identically (0.99 similarity) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Substantial segments are also quoted in the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Paramatthadīpanī* / *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, particularly segments §0.3–15.4), while closing stock verses (§15.1–17.1) are shared with numerous other elder apadānas, including those of Mahāmoggallāna (Tha-Ap 4), Piṇḍolabhāradvāja (Tha-Ap 10), and Upāli (Tha-Ap 8) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring machine alignments with Tibetan canonical sūtras (*Mahāhrāda-sūtra*, D 208, and *Ratnajāliparipṛcchā*, D 163) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
